focus: Source/TitanAI.cs: postfix on Pawn_JobTracker.DetermineNextConstantThinkTreeJob issuing ability jobs with InterruptForced every 30 ticks; risks: job loops, null ConstantThinkTree, lastJobGiver save/load, wild animals casting
diffSource: since build 29 (2026-10-06T04:40:36Z), the last reviewed build, from the build log

findings.title: Postfix issues jobs for pawns with no constant think tree, and those jobs throw when a save loads
findings.detail: Vanilla DetermineNextConstantThinkTreeJob returns NoJob straight away when pawn.thinker?.ConstantThinkTree is null. The postfix runs anyway and can set a valid result. JobTrackerTickInterval then starts the job with thinkTree = ConstantThinkTree (null), so job.jobGiverThinkTree is null and jobGiverKey is -2 (Instance never had a key assigned). On load, Job.ExposeData PostLoadInit calls jobGiverThinkTree.TryGetThinkNodeWithSaveKey(-2) on null and throws. Add the same guard vanilla uses as the first line of Patch_TitanAbilityAI.Postfix: `if (___pawn.thinker?.ConstantThinkTree == null) return;`.

findings.title: JobGiver_TitanAbilities.Instance has no save key, so every titan saved mid-cast logs a warning on load
findings.detail: ThinkNode.uniqueSaveKeyInt defaults to -2 and only ThinkTreeKeyAssigner sets it, which never happens for a node created with new. Job saves jobGiver.UniqueSaveKey (-2) and on load looks it up in jobGiverThinkTree (the pawn's constant tree), fails, and logs 'Could not find think node with key -2'. Jobs from a trait's aiThinkTree are also recorded against Instance, because ThinkNode_JobGiver.TryIssueJobPackage wraps them with `this`. In the postfix, set `__result = new ThinkResult(r.Job, ___pawn.thinker.ConstantThinkNodeRoot, r.Tag, r.FromQueue);` so the saved key resolves to a node in that tree.

findings.title: Postfix runs outside vanilla's try/catch, so an exception in a content mod's aiThinkTree or effect comp reaches the pawn tick
findings.detail: Vanilla runs the constant tree inside try/catch and recovers with JobUtility.TryStartErrorRecoverJob. The postfix runs after that try/catch has finished. An exception thrown by a trait's aiThinkTree or a comp's AICanTargetNow would escape into JobTrackerTickInterval and repeat every 30 ticks for that pawn. Wrap the TryIssueJobPackage call in Patch_TitanAbilityAI.Postfix in try/catch and log with Log.ErrorOnce keyed per pawn or def.

findings.title: Offensive branch skips vanilla's own-cell check before casting
findings.detail: JobGiver_AIFightEnemy.GetAbilityJob only returns an ability job when pawn.Position is walkable and its destination can be reserved. TitanAI.cs step 2 says it picks abilities 'the same way' but has no such gate. Adding the same check before the step-2 loop would match vanilla.

findings.title: Wild titans rarely cast; the settings hint promises more
findings.detail: CurrentEnemy requires t.HostileTo(pawn). For a wild animal that is only true when it is manhunting (mental state), there is predator hostility, or a hostileToAll kind is involved. A wild titan that is merely attacked by a colonist will usually not count them as hostile, so TF_Settings_AbilityAIHint's 'Wild, hostile and tamed titans cast their trait abilities in a fight' overstates wild behaviour. Either reword the hint or accept this as intended.

findings.title: A cast that fails before its cooldown starts would interrupt the pawn every 30 ticks
findings.detail: Repeats are otherwise limited: CanActNow skips pawns whose current job is an ability, cooldowns gate the next cast, and ShouldStartJobFromThinkTree stops a continuing job from restarting. But if an ability job ends at start (for example, line of sight lost after CanHitTarget), no cooldown starts and the next 30-tick pass interrupts the fight job again. The cadence is the same as vanilla's constant-tree job givers, so this is low risk; a short per-pawn retry delay after a failed cast would close it. Opinion, not tested.
